# fivenines_qemu_vms (Data Source)

The libvirt domains on a KVM host: which VM is shut off and since when, what it is assigned, and what it is currently using.

THE METRIC VALUES ARE FRESHNESS-GATED. `cpu_percent` and the five fields beside it are denormalized SAMPLES and come back null once `metrics_fresh` is false, rather than as the last known number -- otherwise a dead agent would leave a VM reading "42% CPU" forever. A null there is "no current sample", never "idle".

THIS IS THE ONLY COLLECTOR THAT CAN REPORT A DELETION. Everywhere else a row the agent stops reporting is deleted, so a sync built on the list alone cannot see it go. A VM removed from libvirt is TOMBSTONED instead: the row stays with `vanished_at` set and clears itself if the VM comes back. **This data source deliberately does NOT filter tombstones out by default**, even though every dashboard surface does -- hiding them is how a sync silently misses the removal it most needed to see. Set `vanished = false` for parity with the UI.

Staleness is org-parameterized on this collector: it is the ORGANIZATION's offline threshold, not the fixed ten minutes the others use.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Tombstones are included by default -- this is the only collector that can
# report a deletion, and hiding them is how a sync misses the removal it most
# needed to see.
data "fivenines_qemu_vms" "all" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.kvm_host.id
}

output "vanished_vms" {
  value = [
    for v in data.fivenines_qemu_vms.all.qemu_vms :
    ({ uuid = v.vm_uuid, name = v.vm_name, vanished_at = v.vanished_at }) if v.vanished
  ]
}

# Set vanished = false for parity with the dashboard.
data "fivenines_qemu_vms" "present" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.kvm_host.id
  vanished    = false
}

# The metric values are freshness-gated: cpu_percent comes back null once
# metrics_fresh is false, rather than as a stale "42%" forever.
output "vm_cpu" {
  value = {
    for v in data.fivenines_qemu_vms.present.qemu_vms :
    v.vm_uuid => v.cpu_percent if v.metrics_fresh
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the VM name or its libvirt UUID.
- `stale` (Boolean) Freshness filter, built on the ORGANIZATION's offline threshold rather than a fixed window -- QEMU rows are refreshed on the org's own collection cadence. `false` returns only rows refreshed inside it; `true` returns the rest. Omit for both.
- `status` (String) The libvirt domain state, in libvirt's own vocabulary. `unknown` is a real value -- what an unrecognized state code maps to -- and does NOT mean the VM is gone (that is `vanished`). One of: `unknown`, `nostate`, `running`, `shutoff`, `paused`, `shutdown`, `crashed`, `pmsuspended`, `idle`.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed. This collector is the ONE EXCEPTION to the no-tombstone rule: a VM removed from libvirt keeps its row with `vanished_at` set, so a sync CAN see a deletion here.
- `vanished` (Boolean) Tombstone filter. `false` returns only VMs still present in libvirt, which is what every dashboard surface shows; `true` returns only the ones that disappeared. **Omitting it returns BOTH, which is this data source's default** and the reason an inventory sync can see a removal here at all.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `qemu_vms` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--qemu_vms))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--qemu_vms"></a>
### Nested Schema for `qemu_vms`

Read-Only:

- `cpu_percent` (Number) Freshness-gated: NULL once `metrics_fresh` is false, rather than the last known value. Null is "no current sample", never "idle".
- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `disk_read_bytes_per_sec` (Number) Freshness-gated: NULL once `metrics_fresh` is false, rather than the last known value. Null is "no current sample", never "idle".
- `disk_write_bytes_per_sec` (Number) Freshness-gated: NULL once `metrics_fresh` is false, rather than the last known value. Null is "no current sample", never "idle".
- `host_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID this row belongs to.
- `id` (String) The row's primary key, which is a UUID -- `qemu_vms` is a `id: :uuid` table. Use `vm_uuid` to address a VM anywhere else in the product; this key is only useful for matching rows between two responses of this API.
- `last_synced_at` (String) Server arrival time of the tick that last refreshed this row (never the agent's clock). Null when the row has never synced.
- `memory_assigned_bytes` (Number) Bytes ASSIGNED, not used.
- `metrics_fresh` (Boolean) Whether the denormalized sample is inside its five-minute window. This is the field that makes a null metric value explainable rather than merely absent -- read it before concluding a VM is idle.
- `metrics_sampled_at` (String) When the gated values above were last sampled.
- `net_rx_bytes_per_sec` (Number) Freshness-gated: NULL once `metrics_fresh` is false, rather than the last known value. Null is "no current sample", never "idle".
- `net_tx_bytes_per_sec` (Number) Freshness-gated: NULL once `metrics_fresh` is false, rather than the last known value. Null is "no current sample", never "idle".
- `ram_percent` (Number) Freshness-gated: NULL once `metrics_fresh` is false, rather than the last known value. Null is "no current sample", never "idle".
- `stale` (Boolean) The row has not been refreshed inside the ORGANIZATION's offline threshold -- NOT the fixed ten minutes the other collectors use. QEMU rows are refreshed on the org's own collection cadence, so a fixed window would call a slow-interval org's healthy VMs stale.
- `state_changed_at` (String) When `status` last CHANGED -- the field that turns "it is shutoff" into "it has been shutoff since 03:12".
- `status` (String) The libvirt domain state, in libvirt's own vocabulary. `unknown` is a real value -- it is what an unrecognized state code maps to, and means "we could not classify it", not "the VM is gone" (that is `vanished_at`). One of: `unknown`, `nostate`, `running`, `shutoff`, `paused`, `shutdown`, `crashed`, `pmsuspended`, `idle`.
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
- `vanished` (Boolean) Convenience form of `vanished_at` being set.
- `vanished_at` (String) When the VM disappeared from libvirt. A TOMBSTONE, not a deletion: the row is kept for the audit trail and clears itself if the VM comes back. This endpoint does NOT filter these out by default even though every dashboard surface does -- hiding rows is how an inventory sync silently misses a removal. Pass `vanished=false` for parity with the UI.
- `vcpu_count` (Number) vCPUs assigned to the domain. Null when not reported.
- `vm_name` (String) The libvirt domain name. Null when libvirt reported none; `vm_uuid` is the stable identity.
- `vm_uuid` (String) The libvirt UUID -- the durable identity, and what the dashboard puts in URLs. Correlate on this, not on `id`.
